 Oh My Romantasy! ‘The Remarried Empress’ Will Leave You Clutching Your Chest (and balling your Fists)
 Sherin Nicole 
 |
 Nov 2, 2026 • 4:30PM 
 FIRST 3 EPISODES REVIEW 
 Friends, I’m not sure where to start. I could go with two of my favorite K-dramas , Oh My Venus starring Shin Min Ah , and While You Were Sleeping starring Lee Jong Suk . Or maybe we should talk about epic fantasy romance , because this isn’t quite a sageuk (a South Korean historical drama). Then again, maybe we should talk about the hit original WEBTOON , with nearly 3 billion views worldwide.
 Yes, let’s start there. In a few days, Hulu will transport us into an all-new royal romance, based on the web novel & manhwa written by Alphatart , starring Shin Min Ah, Ju Jihoon, Lee Jong Suk, and Lee Se Young. The Remarried Empress is a different kind of K-drama, as fantastical and breathless as our favorite romantasies, set in a European-inspired fairytale world of myth , magic , fated love, and warring ambitions.
 Ju Jihoon and Shin Min Ah as Emperor Sovieshu and Empress Navier 
 The jewel in this crown is Shin Min Ah, giving us every facet of an Empress who’s had to dim her light and is left lonely because of it. Navier (Shin) hasn’t been able to step into her power; otherwise, it might wound the pride of an Emperor who was never her match, Sovieshu ( Ju Jihoon ). Co-dependent and frosty as a cold front, Sovieshu once promised he’d never take a mistress like the emperors before him. He lied.
 The Emperor soon loses his heart to a woman who needs him more than Navier ever did: Rashta ( Lee Se Young ). That’s where things fall apart, and the illusions of a happy marriage shatter. But two can play that game, and when Navier is introduced to the legendary and utterly dashing Crown Prince Heinrey (Lee Jong Suk), the palace intrigue and political machinations get juicy.
 Are you here for it? If not, I bet you will be. The mythology, backstabbing, twists, and backstories in the first 3 episodes of The Remarried Empress will leave you wide-eyed and desperately in need of someone to talk to.
 WHY YOU’LL WANT TO WATCH 
 From Bridgerton to The Gilded Age to the love for the Fourth Wing – Empyrean Series , we love historical opulence that’s dripping in romance. Add the power of a four-way royal love polygon and most of us are seated. Even better, this world is filled with arcane magic, fabled beasts, and competing kingdoms.
 From the first moments, every gesture, every tremor of a hand, and every clingy, passive-aggressive comment hints that something deep and unstable is simmering beneath the placid surface of the Eastern Kingdom’s imperial palace. The palace is known as a happy place, but The Remarried Empress is about to teach us that legend and truth often diverge. Perhaps it’s because no heir has been born, but perhaps no heir has been born because of something else…and the rumors are spreading.
 That’s the setting and drama. Now on to the romance: Oh my, my dear friends of all genders, we’ve only gotten a peek at the loneliness, betrayal, and yearning in the first three chapters, and I’m ready to run a heist at Hulu for more episodes. The chemistry between Empress Navier and Prince Heinrey starts so sweetly, but you have the feeling the first meet-cute, in Episode 3, is only kindling for an upcoming blaze.
 On the opposite side of the throne, Emperor Sovieshu and Rashta are wickedly petty and downright dirty, making us hope they’ll eventually destroy each other. I mean, there’s nothing more enjoyable than watching a villain be destroyed by their own traps ( Along the lines of a Purple Wedding for Joffrey ? Quite right.) Although, I must admit there will be times when you’ll hope Rashta gets her lick back, also known as revenge, and enjoy every taste of the sweet life. Just don’t count on that sentiment lasting long.
 Time, time for some, time for some action. The hunting and chase scenes will get your BPMs up like cardio. Like the rest of the series, the set pieces are shot like you’re at the window to another world, and it’s easy to get pulled in.
 For sci-fi and fantasy lovers, imagine a fairytale swashbuckler with a touch of DUNE , a sprinkle of Bridgerton , and a wink at The Witcher , set on an alternate magical Earth, where romance is at the core of the intrigue and the dynamics, both political and personal.
 Finally, there are the visuals. The Remarried Empress is gorgeous, filled with both decadence and danger. Director Cho Suwon (also listed as Jo Soo-won) and the creative team give us a world that’s fascinating and familiar, shooting expansive scenes that revel in the full scope of this world and the wealth of the royal families. The series also contrasts the lush life with the cruelty and harm of enslavement.
 However, I’m not fully sold on the costuming. At times it’s uneven in its anachronistic mix of Western eras and styles. I started wishing they’d gone for a fanciful blend of traditional Korean clothes, jewels, and hair combined with Western looks to create something wholly new. That would have upped the otherworldly aura by ten. Still, the only disappointment is that we have to wait an entire week for episodes 5 and 6.
 IN THE END 
 The Remarried Empress feels like you’re watching through a window to another world; it’s easy to get pulled into the drama, magic, deception, and romance. If you know this cast, you know it’s filled with some of K-drama’s best. If you don’t recognize them, you’re about to have a discovery. No emotion or micro-expression is left unfelt until we are smiling, trembling, and gasping with our dear Empress.
 The Remarried Empress arrives Wed, Nov 4, with a four-episode premiere followed by two new episodes every Wednesday, with the finale on Nov 25. 
 Rating:  B+ 
Level of Enthusiasm:  93% 
 The Remarried Empress premieres Nov 4 on Hulu

 CREDITS: 
 Starring Shin Mina ( Karma, Hometown Cha-Cha-Cha ) as Empress Navier
 Lee Jongsuk ( Big Mouth ) as Crown Prince Heinrey
 Ju Jihoon ( Light Shop, The Trauma Code: Heroes on Call ) as Emperor Sovieshu
 Lee Seyoung ( The Red Sleeve, The Crowned Clown ) as enslaved escapee  Rashta
 The Remarried Empress 
 Adapted for the screen by Yeoh Geena and Hyun Choongyeol 
 Directed by Cho Suwon ( Still 17, Pinocchio )
 Synopsis from HULU / Disney+ 
 Beloved Empress Navier of the Eastern Empire has built and led a prosperous land alongside her husband, Emperor Sovieshu. One day her world is sha ered when the emperor brings Rashta, a runaway slave, back to the palace with the intention of making her his concubine.
 Even as the threat of a broken future looms over her, Navier refuses to let her emotions sway her, and when Prince Heinrey, a rival leader  om the Western Kingdom, shows his interest, Navier will make a life-changing decision to rewrite her destiny.
 First Four Episode Descriptions: 
 Episode 101 
 Emperor Sovieshu and Empress Navier have almost everything they could want in life, but when a runaway enslaved woman is brought into the palace, their perfect lives suddenly come under threat
 Episode 102 
 As the emperor falls for Rashta and works to set her free (after all, she is wholly dependent on him, unlike the Empress), rumors begin to swirl, and Navier stands firm. Meanwhile, news of Prince Heinrey’s impending visit stirs excitement in the palace.
 Episode 103 
 As the New Year’s Ceremony begins, conflict deepens among Navier, Sovieshu, and Rashta. Emboldened by the emperor’s favor, Rashta grows more emboldened than ever, while the arrival of Prince Heinrey further complicates the tangled relationships within the Imperial Palace. (He’s so dashing with his purple eyes.)
 Episode 104 
 As the New Year’s Ceremony sparks an unexpected attraction that leads to Sovieshu struggling with conflicting emotions. Meanwhile, Rashta discovers the identity of Heinrey’s secret pen pal and plots to throw the palace into chaos (as if she hasn’t already).
